description: Massachusetts weatherization provides home energy efficiency services for households eligible for HEAP. The HEAP application also serves as the weatherization application.
introduction: Massachusetts weatherization provides home energy efficiency services for households eligible for HEAP. The HEAP application also serves as the weatherization application.

who: The local weatherization agency determines the work suitable for the property.
sections.get: Energy efficiency improvements determined by the local agency, followed by inspection of completed work. This is a home service rather than spending money paid to the household.
sections.docs: Have the HEAP application information ready and note drafts, insulation concerns and heating problems. If renting, ask what property owner paperwork is required before arranging work.
sections.apply:
1. Find the agency serving your town through the state weatherization page.
  2. Submit a HEAP application online or through the local energy assistance agency.
  3. Ask to be considered for weatherization and arrange the property assessment.
sections.after: Ask about the assessment queue, access arrangements and approved work. Keep the agency’s inspection information and report any concern about completed work to it.
sections.sources:
• State weatherization application guidance
  • USA Assistance background and screenshots

faqs: Must I submit a separate state WAP application?
The state says a HEAP application also serves as the weatherization application.
Does HEAP approval mean work starts immediately?
Ask the local agency about scheduling and assessment.
Who carries out the program locally?
A network of local agencies administers services.
The local agency inspects completed work.
What number helps find local energy assistance?
The state lists the Cold Relief Heatline at 800-632-8175.

provenance.review_scope: Program purpose, eligibility pathway and application methods; no unverified dollar limits published.
